content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"Yes: the judge treats the absence of a begetting statement in the cited verses as support for holding the defense.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"The text states that before Mary and Joseph came together she was found with child of the Holy Ghost ([L1] Matthew 1:18, 20), with the active begetting verb withheld from Joseph in the record of the generations ([L2] egennēthē in Matthew 1:16). While the challenger demonstrated that Davidic lineage is reckoned according to the flesh ([L1] Romans 1:3; [L3] Acts 2:30), neither text states that Joseph begat the child ([L4]).","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"Phrase: 'That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED'. Readings: (1) it bars only a bare finding that one verse omits the link; (2) it also bars using a single verse's withheld or absent wording as support for HELD. I weighed and adopted the second.","why":"The judge relies on what a verse does not state, namely the withheld begetting verb and the cited texts' silence on Joseph begetting, as a reason for HELD, which K-S2 forbids."}
